newsitem.title: USA: Triton confirms extension of Bumi Field.
newsitem.headline: Triton confirms extension of Bumi Field.

text.p: Triton Energy Ltd said Monday its Bumi North-1 well has successfully tested natural gas from multiple reservoirs, confirming a significant northern extension of the Bumi Field on Block A-18 in the Gulf of Thailand.
The Bumi North-1 is in the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area about 15 kilometers (9 miles) north-northeast of the Bumi-1 discovery well, drilled in late 1996.
On test, the well flowed at a stabilized, maximum combined daily rate of 42 million cubic feet of gas and 362 barrels of condensate from selected intervals.

"We are encouraged by the results of Bumi North-1, which flow tested gas from deep, overpressure zones, as well as from shallow and intermediate zones, all of which have been tested in other Block A-18 wells," said Al Turner, Triton senior vice president, operations.

"The Bumi North-1 is a significant well because it substantiates the areal extent of the Bumi Field, the largest field discovered to date on the block. However, additional appraisal drilling will be required to fully evaluate the extent of the field."

The well was flow tested from 4 intervals between 3,850 and 7,340 feet through choke sizes ranging from 32/64 inch to 80/64 inch. Flowing tubing pressure was between 135 and 970 pounds per square inch, and condensate was 45-57 degrees API gravity, Triton said.
The Bumi North-1 was drilled in about 183 feet of water to a depth of 9,250 feet.

Triton currently is drilling an exploratory well on the untested Samudra prospect in the southwest portion of Block A-18. Following the completion of the Samudra-1 well, plans call for one additional exploratory well, the Raya-1, to be drilled in the central portion of Block A-18 during 1997.

Carigali-Triton Operating Co, the operator, is jointly owned by a subsidiary of Triton and Petronas Carigali (JDA), an exploration and production subsidiary of Malaysian state oil company Petronas. Each hold a 50 percent interest.
